ideas.title: Terminal Collision
ideas.hook: Everyone holds a private Dominion hand and slams cards into one shared turn at the same time, against a single Actions counter on the TV, and the first person to play a card when it hits zero fizzles the whole chain for the room.

ideas.title: Bones File
ideas.hook: Everyone dives their own five-room roguelike on their phone at the same time, and when you die your floor, your angry ghost and your hand-labelled potions get spliced into a living friend's run, labels and all, whether you labelled them honestly or not.

ideas.title: Haul Count
ideas.hook: Rural residents living beside a new sand mine can't prove the dump trucks start at 4 a.m. or run triple their permitted count. Haul Count is a $150 solar camera on a fencepost that counts every loaded truck and produces a dated log formatted for the county permit hearing.

ideas.title: Repair Receipt
ideas.hook: Public-housing tenants report the same ceiling leak for months by phone and have nothing to prove it. Repair Receipt turns a text plus a photo into a timestamped record, sends the landlord a properly cited notice, and counts down the legal deadline.

ideas.title: Not My Debt
ideas.hook: A domestic-violence survivor leaves with $14k of car loans and credit cards an abuser opened in her name, and the advocate helping her has no time to fight each one. Not My Debt reads the survivor's credit report, helps tag each coerced account, and produces the right block, dispute and state coerced-debt letters in one sitting.

ideas.title: Last Swipe
ideas.hook: EBT families find their whole month's SNAP balance drained minutes after it loads, and since federal replacement ended nobody pays them back. Last Swipe gathers the 'where did I last use my card' answers from every victim and clusters them to pinpoint the compromised checkout lane, so the processor can pull the skimmer before the next deposit day.

ideas.title: Out of Sight Discount
ideas.hook: Amazon's fair-pricing bot drops your Buy Box the moment it finds your product cheaper on your own site, so this SaaS shows DTC brands which of their discounts the crawler can actually see and rebuilds each promo in a form it can't price-match, such as member pricing, bundles, or checkout-time codes.

ideas.title: Handshake Tax
ideas.hook: A one-command eBPF probe for your homelab or prod box that counts every TCP+TLS handshake your services redo to hosts they already have connections open to, then bills each service in milliseconds and CPU like an itemized tab.

ideas.title: Nothing to See
ideas.hook: A generator reads all ~70k EasyList cosmetic rules, builds a fake web page made only of elements those rules hide, and paints it as a loud collage, so with your ad blocker on the URL shows a blank white page and with it off you get the mural.

ideas.title: Front of the Line
ideas.hook: You're handed the real mempool from a real Ethereum block and get to be the block builder: reorder it, slip your own trades in, sandwich whoever set sloppy slippage, then see how your take compares to what the actual builder got.

ideas.title: Downdrift
ideas.hook: Draw a coastline, set the prevailing swell, and watch a century of longshore drift run in two minutes: build one groyne to save your favourite beach and see the town downdrift lose its sand by year 40.

ideas.title: The Chair Is a Buffer
ideas.hook: Log the start and stop of your recurring chores for two weeks and get back a Satisfactory-style factory diagram of your household, with the chair of clean unfolded laundry correctly labelled as a work-in-progress buffer and the one station that actually caps your throughput glowing red.

ideas.title: Spiked
ideas.hook: Every phone is a newsroom with a private stack of tips that partly overlap with the other desks. File a story first and you get the front page, but if two desks file the same story within three seconds, the editor spikes both as duplicates.

ideas.title: Gift Receipt
ideas.hook: One player is the birthday guest and the rest secretly shop from different torn-off slices of their wishlist. Any two identical gifts both get returned on the spot, and since the guest is sitting right there listening, saying 'I've got the headphones' out loud spoils the surprise and halves that gift.

ideas.title: Guard Bench
ideas.hook: One lifeguard calls in sick and a pool shuts its lap lanes on the swim club that already paid for them. Guard Bench is a shared, cert-verified substitute pool across city, YMCA and school pools, so the shift gets filled instead of cancelled.

ideas.title: Lot Check
ideas.hook: Food pantries hand out donated canned goods, baby formula and pain relievers with no realistic way to check each one against this week's recalls. Lot Check lets a volunteer scan the barcode, type or photograph the lot code, and get a red or green answer against FDA, USDA and CPSC enforcement data.

ideas.title: Desk Check
ideas.hook: A five-person startup ships a laptop to a 'remote engineer' and has no way to know it's sitting on a shelf in a Texas laptop farm with 40 others. Desk Check is a tiny agent that reports where the laptop really lives, whether it's being driven by a KVM, and whether it's on a network shared with other companies' fleets.

ideas.title: Still Waiting
ideas.hook: Families wait years on housing-voucher lists and then get purged because one 'are you still interested?' letter went to an old address. Still Waiting tracks every list a client is on, catches each purge window, and has their caseworker answer before the deadline.

ideas.title: Message Received
ideas.hook: One scout knows tonight is safe, and confirmation messages pass phone to phone but one in four quietly vanishes. Everyone has to hit ATTACK in the same two seconds, and no number of "got it"s ever makes you sure.

ideas.title: Same Corner
ideas.hook: Every phone shows the same unlabeled maze of dots and lines, but each one is scrambled, rotated and mirrored differently. Without talking, everyone has to walk their token to the same dot, and "top left" means nothing because no two screens agree.

ideas.title: Told Me Different
ideas.hook: Only the map-holder sees the maze, and they send each piece directions over a private channel while secretly trying to walk one hidden victim into the pit, so the pieces have to check their directions against the four walls each of them can feel and catch the lie before it's too late.

ideas.title: Press Square
ideas.hook: The map-holder sees four identical grey dots and four colored exits, and each piece's phone has four unlabeled shape buttons wired to a secret direction, so the map-holder has to work out who is which dot and what each button does while the shared move budget runs out.

ideas.title: Nobody in Particular
ideas.hook: The room fills in one group census poster where every column is your own private answer and every blur you add costs the poster ink. Your friends then try to link your row to you using what they already know, and any row they unmask gets blacked out of the keepsake.

ideas.title: Someone Paid
ideas.hook: Four phones run a real dining-cryptographers network, so the room types an anonymous card onto a shared tape one letter per second and nobody, not even the server, can tell who wrote what. Two people typing in the same slot leave an ink blot, and the only way to avoid one is to say out loud that you are typing.

ideas.title: Downstream
ideas.hook: Your Mac wallpaper becomes a live Navier–Stokes fluid where every open window is a solid obstacle — drag a window and you stir the desktop, leave Slack open in the current and it sheds a lazy Kármán vortex street behind it all day.

ideas.title: Read It Before
ideas.hook: A cryptomnesia checker that scans your draft against everything you've actually read — browser history, Readwise highlights, saved PDFs — and flags the sentence you think is yours but is really a half-remembered line from a blog post you read in March.

ideas.title: Pass Blame
ideas.hook: Your benchmark got slower at -O2 — this CLI binary-searches LLVM's own optimization pipeline, pass by pass, and names the exact pass invocation that made your hot loop worse.
